actions.action: Cut the woody stalk back to just above a node with leaves or a visible bud
Alternatively, remove the woody stalk entirely at the soil line or above the lowest leaf cluster
Prune stems just above a pair of leaves when harvesting
Pinch off flower buds as they form
Keep the larger seedling and gently remove or transplant the others
Check the tiny plant at the bottom to confirm it is basil and not a weed

reason: The answer identifies the woody, overgrown stalk as a pruning problem and advises removing or cutting back the stalk and pruning above leaf nodes, which matches the fix that worked, with nothing harmful.
